content.title: 11.3.10 Short-term mechanical circulatory support
content.summary: Guidance on use of short-term mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in patients with cardiogenic shock to augment cardiac output and support end-organ perfusion. Short-term MCS may be used as bridge-to-recovery (BTR), bridge-to-decision (BTD) or bridge-to-bridge/bridge-to-transplant (BTB). Unselected use is not supported; implantation and management require specialist multidisciplinary expertise.
key_points: Short-term MCS can be used as a BTR, BTD or BTB to support patients with cardiogenic shock.
Initial improvements in cardiac output, blood pressure and arterial lactate may be offset by significant complications; high-quality outcome evidence is limited.

Unselected routine use of MCS in cardiogenic shock is not supported; specialist multidisciplinary teams and standardized team-based approaches with predefined algorithms and monitoring may improve outcomes.

Intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) is not routinely recommended post-myocardial infarction (post-MI) cardiogenic shock based on the IABP-SHOCK-II trial, which showed no difference in 30-day or long-term mortality between IABP and optimal medical therapy (OMT) after acute MI with early revascularization.

Other short-term devices and veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) have mixed or limited data; VA-ECMO may be considered in fulminant myocarditis and severe cardiogenic shock but can increase left ventricular (LV) afterload and may require LV unloading (e.g., transseptal/ventricular apex vent or unloading devices such as Impella).

trials_and_evidence.name: IABP-SHOCK-II
trials_and_evidence.finding: No difference in 30-day or long-term mortality between IABP and OMT in patients with cardiogenic shock following acute MI who underwent early revascularization.
trials_and_evidence.implication: IABP is not routinely recommended in cardiogenic shock post-MI but may be considered in selected cases (e.g., not due to ACS, refractory to drug therapy) as BTD, BTR, or BTB.

trials_and_evidence.name: Meta-analyses/Observational studies
trials_and_evidence.finding: Some meta-analyses and observational data suggest favourable outcomes for VA-ECMO compared to controls in cardiogenic shock or cardiac arrest, but randomized data are lacking or inconclusive.
trials_and_evidence.implication: Consider VA-ECMO in selected severe cases; monitor for increased LV afterload and consider unloading strategies.

recommendations_table.recommendation: Short-term MCS should be considered in patients with cardiogenic shock as a BTR, BTD, BTB. Further indications include treatment of the cause of cardiogenic shock or long-term MCS or transplantation.

IABP may be considered in patients with cardiogenic shock as a BTR, BTD, BTB, including treatment of the cause of cardiogenic shock (e.g., mechanical complication of acute MI) or long-term MCS or transplantation.
IABP is not routinely recommended in post-MI cardiogenic shock.

content.notes: When VA-ECMO is used, assess severity of myocardial dysfunction and valvular lesions; LV unloading may be mandatory in some cases. Standardized team-based approaches with invasive haemodynamic monitoring, lactate, and markers of end-organ damage are suggested to potentially improve survival.
